transcript:
Header: 2025-11-05 15:00 PST | Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Malik (Redwood AE), Daniel Chen (Redwood SE), Robert Hale (Quantica CTO), Priya Sethi (Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Infra Lead)

Summary (auto): Discussed Dedicated reserved capacity, burst windows, and compliance needs. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmarks, and infra deep-dive.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): hey everyone thanks for taking the time, i'm aisha with redwood inference, uh joined by daniel our se. quick roll call?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Robert): hey this is robert, thanks, priya and marco are with me. quick context: we're building a real-time underwriting product, inference at the 100 qps peak range with tight p95 latency targets.
00:36 Speaker 1 (Aisha): perfect, and you flagged dedicated as the primary option in the form — is that for isolation, perf, or both?
00:48 Speaker 3 (Priya): primarily isolation; we can't send data to multi-tenant hosts because of regulatory obligations. also cost predictability for sustained traffic. but also need low latency for scoring.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Daniel): okay good; can you give us the traffic shape? sustained baseline, burst multipliers, seq length distribution etc.
01:18 Speaker 3 (Priya): baseline 20 qps, spikes up to 120 qps for a few hours after market opens. average prompt length ~150 tokens, longest about 600 for certain reports.
01:35 Speaker 4 (Marco): infra note — we run on GCP today, we have peered VPCs and strict egress controls. we'd prefer private deployment or dedicated in a customer VPC.
01:52 Speaker 2 (Daniel): good to know. with dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools with optional burst capacity into shared pools; bursts can be limited by policy. do you have any SLA or latency SLOs you need?
02:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): p95 latency should be under 350ms for the 150-token case. cost is secondary but still important.
02:24 Speaker 1 (Aisha): ok so two axes: sizing for your baseline sustained qps and policies for short-term bursts. usually we'll recommend sizing to handle baseline with headroom and using burst pool for transient peaks.
02:38 Speaker 2 (Daniel): technical detail — what models are you planning to serve? open models, or fine-tuned heavier ones? model choice affects GPU memory and batch behavior a lot.
02:50 Speaker 3 (Priya): we plan to start with a 13B fine-tuned model for classification, possibly move to a 33B for better cal calibration.
03:02 Speaker 2 (Daniel): right, 13B vs 33B changes the recommended instance types and quantization options. for dedicated we can provide optimized kernels and quantized variants to reduce footprint.
03:18 Speaker 4 (Marco): also curious about caching — prefix/KV cache could help for repeated contexts, do you support sticky caching across requests?
03:32 Speaker 2 (Daniel): yes we have prefix and KV cache features; the cache is local to the serving pool but with Dedicated we can configure longer-lived caches. note transcription: sometimes KV cache appears as K V cash in older exports — ignore that.
03:50 Speaker 1 (Aisha): can we talk about security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), RBAC, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and audit logs retained for one year.
04:05 Speaker 2 (Daniel): we support SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS integrations. for Private deployments we can do a customer-managed control plane and HSM integration, audit logs to your SIEM. retention windows are configurable as an add-on.
04:22 Speaker 3 (Priya): great, for procurement we need a security package and a shared responsibility matrix.
04:30 Speaker 1 (Aisha): we'll send that — daniel will attach our security whitepaper and the KMS integration guide.
04:38 Speaker 2 (Daniel): back to capacity: usually we size GPUs by tokens/sec and model memory. e.g., for a 13B quantized we might need 8x A10 equivalent for baseline, but that depends on concurrency and batching.
04:55 Speaker 4 (Marco): do you support autoscaling? we can't have cold starts that increase latency on scale-up.
05:08 Speaker 2 (Daniel): autoscaling on Dedicated is policy-driven; you can do reserved capacity + controlled autoscale with pre-warmed instances. we also support burst queues that will route to compatible model variants if needed to maintain availability.
05:24 Speaker 3 (Priya): so in a spike if the reserved pool is saturated, requests can either queue, fall back to a smaller quantized model, or spill into a burst pool? which is default?
05:38 Speaker 2 (Daniel): defaults are configurable. common pattern: try reserved pool first, then burst pool, then fallback to lower-cost model variant for non-critical flows. for latency-critical flows we recommend larger reserved pools to avoid fallback.
05:55 Speaker 1 (Aisha): pricing note — reserved capacity is committed monthly or annually; bursts from shared pools are metered. we'll include SKU examples in the pricing doc.
06:08 Speaker 4 (Marco): networking detail — we need VPC peering and private egress with route controls, also mutual TLS for internal traffic.
06:22 Speaker 2 (Daniel): supported; for Private deployment we can do on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane, and mutual TLS for service-to-service.
06:32 Speaker 3 (Priya): what's the typical lead time for Dedicated provisioning?
06:40 Speaker 1 (Aisha): usually 2-4 weeks for capacity provisioning depending on region and GPU availability; on-prem takes longer.
06:50 Speaker 4 (Marco): any recommended observability hooks? we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-model latencies.
06:58 Speaker 2 (Daniel): yes Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, and tracing. we can also stream metrics to your Grafana/Prometheus.
07:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): do you have examples for canary rollouts and automatic fallback? we have strict quality gating for new model versions.
07:22 Speaker 2 (Daniel): rollouts supported — canary, A/B, automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to eval sets. we'll share a rollout playbook.
07:36 Speaker 1 (Aisha): any procurement constraints, contract length preferences?
07:40 Speaker 2 (Robert): procurement prefers annual commitments but wants flexibility to add burst capacity; also requires an SLA for latency.
07:52 Speaker 4 (Marco): and legal wants data residency notes — all logs for EU customer traffic must stay in EU region.
08:02 Speaker 2 (Daniel): region pinning is supported; Dedicated pools can be region-specific and routing policies can enforce residency.
08:12 Speaker 1 (Aisha): ok to wrap with next steps.
08:18 Speaker 3 (Priya): quick question on benchmarking — do you run perf runs with our dataset or synthetic?
08:26 Speaker 2 (Daniel): we prefer a hybrid: synthetic to validate baseline throughput and then a short run with your representative prompts to measure p95 and memory behavior. we'll send a benchmark checklist.
08:38 Speaker 1 (Aisha): recap: we'll send pricing, security docs, benchmark checklist, and propose a deep-dive slot. you (Quantica) will share traffic profile and sample prompts.
08:50 Speaker 2 (Robert): sounds good. thanks everyone.
08:55 Speaker 1 (Aisha): thanks, we'll follow up via email with attachments and calendar invite for the deep dive.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-recognitions (K V cache -> KV cache, model names sometimes truncated). References: security whitepaper (link to be attached), pricing SKU spreadsheet, benchmark checklist (to be shared).
